To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed a combination of domain adaptation techniques based GANs and features based strategies that takes into consideration the category level adaptation and it is able to improve the performance of semantic segmentation models learned on synthetic data and applied on real images.

the proposed combination of domain adaptation techniques can be useful in cases in which the amount of annotated images is limited and that it is possible to improve the semantic segmentation accuracy by using the information provided by the synthetic data.

1) the combination of GANs with adaptive features can boost the performance of semantic segmentation models trained on synthetic data; 2) a category level adaptation can be useful to improve domain transfer in case of limited real data; 3) self-supervision can improve the performance in the case of limited real labeled data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning a semantic segmentation model for real world images from a synthetic dataset, and it proposes a novel combination of domain adaptation techniques based upon GANs
the following questions: How can we exploit synthetic data for training semantic segmentation models? How can we transfer knowledge from synthetic to real data?

the following questions: 1) What are the main challenges of semantic segmentation in real-world applications? 2) How can we use synthetic data for this task? 3) What are the most effective domain adaptation methods?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach can improve the results of a semantic segmentation network when applied on a real world dataset, even in case of limited amount of available real world annotated data.
the proposed approach has shown promising results and it can represent an effective solution for the domain shift between real and synthetic data for semantic segmentation with GANs.
the proposed method is able to improve the semantic segmentation performance in the target domain by a large margin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approach can be used to improve the performance of semantic segmentation models in case of limited amount of real data, which is a very common case for autonomous driving.

the proposed method is able to improve the performance of a model trained on synthetic data when applied to real images and that it is able to reduce the performance drop when compared to models trained on real data.

the proposed method is able to improve the performance on real images with respect to the baseline model learned on synthetic data, but it does not reach the level of the state of the art models learned on real data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a generative model for style transfer can be useful in order to reduce domain gap, but it is not sufficient to obtain a good performance.
the use of GANs is not enough to achieve good performance on real data.

a domain adaptation strategy based on GANs can help in reducing the style shift between synthetic and real data, but it is necessary to combine it with a feature based adaptation that takes into consideration the category level differences.
